recipes.name: Savory Stuffed Chicken Breast with Plum Glaze
ingredients_raw: 2 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat olive oil in a skillet over high heat. Using a paring knife, cut a pocket into the side of each breast. Place into skillet and sear until lightly browned on both sides, but not cooked through. Set aside.
Combine cornbread, bacon, celery, onion, butter, and 1/4 cup chicken stock; mix until well combined. Stuff each breast with cornbread mixture.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes.
While the chicken is baking, bring 1/3 cup chicken stock to a simmer. Whisk in plum jam, and simmer over medium-low heat until most of the chicken stock has evaporated.
Pour plum glaze over chicken breasts, and cook for an additional 10 minutes and the center of the stuffed breast reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Stuffed Chicken Breast with Plum Glaze
raw_recipe.description: Seasoned chicken breasts are stuffed with a cornbread mixture and then basted with a plum glaze. Sweet, savory, simple!

review.reviewBody: This is an edit to my previous review - this recipe has been very well received by everyone who has eaten it. I have made it with peach jam which was too sweet and finally found the plum jam - which was worth looking for - it really made the recipe. I have made it according to the directs, and I have made it as a layered casserole when I felt that stuffing the chicken would be to time intensive. It adapts well to a cardiac diet by using low fat/salt plain cornbread and turkey bacon. I stand by my recommendation that you use a savory cornbread - not a sweet cornbread for the stuffing. Overall a great dish!

This was excellent. I made this tonight for my father's birthday party for 6 people. I used the large boneless chicken breasts with the rib meat to cut a better "pocket." I made 4 times the stuffing and put the extra around the chicken once it was stuffed. I did all the prep work yesterday and since I had to fry 8 pieces of bacon, I saved the grease and use that to brown the chicken. I found the plum jam in the international aisle at the grocery store, it was actually in the Polish section.

I made this for a friend who is allergic to corn, so instead of cornmeal, I used plain cooked couscous. It was fabulous. Next time I think I will try rice stuffing for a different take on this recipe.

Instead of stuffing the chicken breasts, I cut them into bite-size pieces and dipped them in celery seed and minced onion. Then I put them in a baking dish with chicken stock & let sit in refrigerator. Then I discarded the chicken stock and added a little butter to the baking dish and cooked, adding the plum/stock mixture for the last 10 minutes. It smelled, looked, and tasted great!!
Simple and so very delicious. I added 1/4 tsp. of dried thyme to the stuffing and stuffed the chicken prior to browning, then finished in the oven. This is a keeper. Thank you.

This recipe is amazing. plan and simple. I did not have any cellery, so I chopped up a little green bell pepper and it turned out wonderfully. I added a clove of fresh garlic, and one thing that I did do is i doubled the glaze. It made a wonderful sauce to have the chicken in and it made the chicken so moist. I will make this recipe again.

I thought this was a delicious and different twist on chicken. After making this with skinless chicken - I think I would try it next time with skin-on chicken breast to add more flavor and texture with the plum glaze. The stuffing turned out well, I sauteed the onion and celery with the bacon to bring softness to the vegetables. I placed the finished chicken breast on top of a bed of sauteed spinach. The spinach, dressing and chicken combined to make one tasty meal!

This recipe was awesome.Since cornbread stuffing is a seasonal thing I used a boxed chicken stuffing and added three cornbread squares, that I made, to the mixture. You can use more or less to your taste(my husband says more). I could not find the plum jelly so I substitued apricot jam (about 1/4 of the jar) and added 5 prunes chopped up to the mixture while it reduced on the stove. This is a keeper.
I used jalapeno cornbread for the stuffing, chicken tenders. and added cracked pepper for serving.

This was so good! I did use stove top instead of the suggested stuffing mixture becuase i had it on hand. I also added a little white wine to the plum sauce. I seasoned the chicken with dried garlic and onion flakes to give it a little seasoning while baking. My boyfriend loved it!

This was very good! A nice change to baked chicken. I never made stuffing before, can you believe that! And I did for the first time with this recipe and it was great! The plum glaze kind of taste like bbq sauce to me. It was really good. Got it from Walmart right where the other jellies were. All the way on the bottom shelf. I added more seasoning than salt and pepper. Other than that doubled the recipe and it turned out good. Used 1 box of Jiffy for 4 big chicken breast and about 6 slices of bacon. Oh yeah and I used the whole jar of jam and added chicken stock accordingly. We like extra sauce around here. Husband approved of this meal. Thank you
What a delicious and easy recipe. Highly recommend
Simple to make and was very good!
Made as directed and was a hit!!!! I had a lemon-fig jam

Could not find plum jam so had to improvise. by using a apricot, peach and passion fruit jam. My dinner guest didn't think she would care for the mixture but she keep going back for more sauce. I still would like to try it with the plum jam but this was wonderful.
Very easy to make and made homemade cornbread for the stuffing. Delicious!
This dish was incredible! I made it for Valentines Day Dinner. It was one of the best dishes I have ever cooked!
This recipe is SO SO SO GOOD !!! You will not be disappointed
I've made this a few times now. Can't find the plum jam in my store so I've made it with apricot and strawberry. Very tasty...this recipe is a keeper.
Loved this and better still, my husband who doesn't like chicken loved it. The dressing made it with the sauce. Only thing I will try next time is saute onions and celery in the butter.....Great
